title_clean: NIFTY Might Cross 50,000 Within 5 Years - How
summary: Bull-market arithmetic: price = EPS x PE. 2003-07 the Nifty rose ~7x on only ~30% PE expansion (20 to 26), i.e. earnings did the work. With 15-20% EPS compounding plus low-rate-driven PE expansion, a 4x move to 50,000 within five years is arithmetically possible; J-curve effects (IBC, NPA clean-up) support earnings.
lessons: Index price is EPS times PE: doubling EPS with doubling PE gives 4x - the 2003-07 bull was ~90% earnings-driven (PE only 20 to 26).
Low interest rates pull money from deposits into equities and drive PE expansion; high rates do the reverse.
Rupee stability (69 in 2013 to ~73 in 2020 vs 6 to 16 in 1978-86) removes a key reason for India-wide high rates.
Buy 10%+ corrections within a confirmed bull market; corrections of 10-30% occurred even inside the 2003-07 bull.

title_clean: Don't Buy Gold in 2021 Before Watching This!
summary: Gold framework for India: local price = international dollar price x USD/INR + import duty. Duty went 1% (pre-2013) to 10% (2013) to 12.5% (2020), incentivizing smuggling. Since 1973 gold has spiked only three times - 1980 oil crisis, 2008-11 Lehman era to $1,910, 2020 COVID to $2,070 - and mean-reverts once each crisis resolves; calls $3,000 unlikely, advising against gold as an investment.
lessons: Indian gold price decomposes into international price x exchange rate plus import duty - all three must be judged before a view.
Gold spikes only around global crises (1980, 2008-11, 2020) and stalls for years once the crisis resolves - crisis premiums mean-revert.
Import duties high enough (12.5%) incentivize smuggling, which caps further hikes - a policy constraint for the duty trajectory.
A stable rupee removes gold's currency-hedge argument for Indian investors.
